entry.strongs: H120 (ʾāḏām); H376 (ʾîš, with ʾănāšîm as its plural)
entry.lemma: ʾāḏām as the generic collective noun in Isaiah, alone and in the ʾāḏām / ʾîš refrain
entry.literal: human(s), humankind / man, each one, anyone / men, people
entry.standardEnglish: ASV 'the mean man … the great man' (2:9; 5:15), 'man' / 'men' elsewhere; NRSV 'people … everyone' (2:9; 5:15), 'everyone' (2:11), 'mortals … their … they' (2:22); NJPS 'man … mortal'
entry.wohChoice: 'humankind' for ʾāḏām / hā-ʾāḏām used generically (2:9, 11, 17, 20, 22; 5:15; as already printed at 29:19 and 45:12); 'everyone' for ʾîš in the synonymous refrain wayyiššaḥ ʾāḏām wayyišpal-ʾîš ('So humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low', 2:9; 'And humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low', 5:15); 'human' for ʾănāšîm in the parallel colon rûm ʾănāšîm, 'human loftiness' (2:11, 17). Pronoun rule: the collective hā-ʾāḏām takes English plural pronouns, although the Hebrew suffixes and pronouns are singular (2:20 'their idols of silver … which they made for themselves'; 2:22 'who have breath in their nostrils; for of what account are they?'). ʾîš and ʾănāšîm outside the refrain (e.g. 'men of Judah', 5:3, 7) are not governed by this entry. Founder ruling 2026-11-26 (wave I-1 decision 2, option C1).
entry.rationale: In Isa 2 and 5 ʾāḏām is the generic collective for human beings set against YHWH, who 'alone shall be exalted' (2:11, 17), and the book's stable chapters already render it 'humankind' (29:19 'the poorest of humankind'; 45:12 'I created humankind upon it'), the NRSV-type inclusive rendering of the collective. The refrain wayyiššaḥ ʾāḏām wayyišpal-ʾîš (2:9; 5:15) was read by ASV and KJV as a social contrast ('the mean man … the great man'), on the model of bᵉnê ʾāḏām … bᵉnê ʾîš in Ps 49:3 and 62:10; without bᵉnê the nouns are most naturally a synonymous pair, as NRSV, NJPS, Wildberger (Isaiah 1-12, 1991) and Williamson (Isaiah 1-5, ICC, 2006) take them, and BDB records ʾîš in the generic sense 'each, anyone' in parallel with ʾāḏām. The draft rendered the pair 'humankind … man', which set a neutral and a gender-marked English word side by side for two synonyms. The founder ruling of 2026-11-26 (option C1, recommended by the Reviewer) gives ʾîš its generic sense, 'everyone', as NRSV does ('people … everyone'), so the line reads 'humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low' at both 2:9 and 5:15. In the parallel colon of 2:11 and 2:17, rûm ʾănāšîm ('the loftiness of men'; ʾănāšîm serves as the plural of ʾîš) is rendered 'human loftiness'. The alternative 'the loftiness of all people' was considered and not adopted, because the Hebrew has no kol 'all'; the adjective keeps the parallel with 'humankind' and adds no word. The pronoun rule follows from the same ruling: the collective hā-ʾāḏām takes English plural pronouns. At 2:20 the plural verb ʿāśû already governs the relative clause, so the singular suffixes of kaspô, zᵉhāḇô and lô are rendered 'their … themselves' (NRSV, ASV); at 2:22 the singular bᵉʾappô and hûʾ are rendered 'their nostrils … are they' (NRSV 'who have only breath in their nostrils … of what account are they?'). Both rules are standard English practice for a Hebrew collective and change no sense. The central entries are not applied: ha-adam ('the human') is scoped to Genesis 2-3, where the article marks the first human, and adam-adamah is applied in Isaiah only at ʾădāmāh 'ground' sites. The entry is direct because every rendering is attested in the standard versions and no reading is added. ISA-5:15 is governed here; the chapter 5 Editor proposed no separate entry.
entry.rendering: 'humankind' for ʾāḏām / hā-ʾāḏām used generically (2:9, 11, 17, 20, 22; 5:15; as already printed at 29:19 and 45:12); 'everyone' for ʾîš in the synonymous refrain wayyiššaḥ ʾāḏām wayyišpal-ʾîš ('So humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low', 2:9; 'And humankind is bowed down, and everyone is brought low', 5:15); 'human' for ʾănāšîm in the parallel colon rûm ʾănāšîm, 'human loftiness' (2:11, 17). Pronoun rule: the collective hā-ʾāḏām takes English plural pronouns, although the Hebrew suffixes and pronouns are singular (2:20 'their idols of silver … which they made for themselves'; 2:22 'who have breath in their nostrils; for of what account are they?'). ʾîš and ʾănāšîm outside the refrain (e.g. 'men of Judah', 5:3, 7) are not governed by this entry. Founder ruling 2026-11-26 (wave I-1 decision 2, option C1).

entry.lemma: hāḏār 'splendour, adornment' in construct with gāʾôn 'majesty, eminence'
entry.standardEnglish: the glory of his majesty (ASV, NRSV); his dread majesty (NJPS)
entry.wohChoice: 'the splendor of his majesty' (2:10, 19, 21): hāḏār 'splendor' (as at 53:2 'no splendor'), gāʾôn 'majesty' (as at 24:14 'the majesty of YHWH'); 'glory' is reserved for kāḇôḏ.
entry.rationale: hāḏār is 'ornament, splendour, honour' (BDB; HALOT; Warmuth, TDOT 3:335-341), and gāʾôn is 'height, eminence, majesty' (BDB; HALOT); ASV's 'the glory of his majesty' is a fair English rendering in isolation. In this corpus, however, 'glory' is the fixed English for kāḇôḏ (central kavod-yhwh, applied at Isa 40:5), and Isaiah sets the two nouns side by side in a single verse ('the glory of Lebanon … the splendour of Carmel … the glory of YHWH, the splendour of our God', 35:2), so a shared English word would hide a distinction the Hebrew draws. The stable chapters already render hāḏār 'splendor' (53:2) and gāʾôn 'majesty' (24:14), and the change keeps the book concordant. 'Splendor' is a standard lexical gloss of hāḏār and carries no interpretive load, so the claim is direct.
entry.rendering: 'the splendor of his majesty' (2:10, 19, 21): hāḏār 'splendor' (as at 53:2 'no splendor'), gāʾôn 'majesty' (as at 24:14 'the majesty of YHWH'); 'glory' is reserved for kāḇôḏ.

entry.lemma: śᵉḵiyyāh, a hapax of disputed sense; with ḥemdāh 'desire, delight'
entry.partOfSpeech: noun (feminine plural, construct) + noun with article
entry.standardEnglish: pleasant imagery (ASV); pleasant pictures (KJV); the beautiful craft (NRSV); the gallant barks (NJPS)
entry.wohChoice: 'all the beautiful vessels' (2:16), in parallel with 'all the ships of Tarshish'.
entry.rationale: The noun occurs only here. ASV and KJV derive it from śkh 'look' (compare maśkîṯ 'carved figure', Lev 26:1; Num 33:52) and render 'pleasant imagery / pictures'. Modern lexicography connects it with an Egyptian word for a ship and reads the line as synonymous parallelism with ʾŏniyyôṯ taršîš 'ships of Tarshish' (HALOT s.v.; Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12, 1991; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000); NRSV ('the beautiful craft') and NJPS ('the gallant barks') follow, and the LXX 'every sight of beautiful ships' already combines both senses. As with the Akkadian loanword at 40:20 (lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah), the revised identification is adopted because the Masoretic consonants support it without emendation. 'Vessels' is chosen over NRSV 'craft' to keep a separate English word from 'ships' and to stay unambiguously nautical, since 'craft' in present-day English also denotes aircraft; the lens-salient reading of this site is confined to a labelled apparatus note. The claim is inferred rather than direct because the loanword etymology is a well-supported proposal, not a certainty, and the traditional English versions read otherwise.
entry.rendering: 'all the beautiful vessels' (2:16), in parallel with 'all the ships of Tarshish'.

entry.translit: bᵉrōʾš; nāhărû; hôḵîaḥ lᵉ-; ʾittîm; mālᵉʾû miqqedem; yaśpîqû; nāṭaštāh; wᵉšāp̄ēl; laʿărōṣ; laḥpōr pērôṯ
entry.strongs: H7218 (rōʾš); H5102 (nāhar); H3198 (ykḥ); H855 (ʾēṯ); H6924 (qedem); H5606 (spq); H5203 (nṭš); H8213 (šāp̄ēl); H6206 (ʿāraṣ); H2661 + H6512 (Strong's follows the two-word division at 2:20)
entry.lemma: single-site lexical and textual decisions of Isaiah 2
entry.literal: at the head of; they shall stream; arbitrate for; ploughing tools; they are full from the east; they clap / abound; you have forsaken; and low; to terrify; to dig holes / to moles
entry.standardEnglish: ASV throughout; NRSV 'as the highest of', 'stream', 'arbitrate', 'to terrify'; NJPS 'gaze with joy', 'abound', 'overawe', 'flying foxes'
entry.wohChoice: 2:2 'on the top of the mountains … shall flow to it' (ASV); 2:4 'shall decide for many peoples … plowshares' (ASV/NJPS); 2:6 'they are full from the east' with no supplement, 'they strike hands with' (spq I), MT 2ms 'you have forsaken' kept; 2:12 MT wᵉšāp̄ēl 'and it shall be brought low' kept (emendation gāḇōah in commentary); 2:19, 21 laʿărōṣ 'to terrify' (NRSV; ASV 'shake mightily'); 2:20 one-word reading laḥăp̄arpērôṯ 'to the moles' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS) against the Leningrad two-word division (founder sign-off 2026-11-26).
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator flagged a choice between standard renderings; the Editor keeps the Masoretic text and the ASV wording unless the lexicon or the Masoretic consonants support a change. (1) bᵉrōʾš hehārîm is spatial 'on the top of' (BDB rōʾš), and nhr I 'flow, stream' is preferred to NJPS nhr II 'be radiant' because the parallel Mic 4:1 and the uphill-stream image are read so by most commentators (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp). (2) The Hiphil of ykḥ with lᵉ- is to decide or arbitrate for parties (BDB; HALOT); ʾittîm is a digging or ploughing implement whose exact form is unknown (ploughshare, mattock or hoe have all been proposed), and 'plowshares' is kept as the English of all three standard versions. (3) At 2:6 the elliptical mālᵉʾû miqqedem is translated without ASV's supplement or the conjectural qōsᵉmîm; spq I 'clap, strike hands' (Job 27:23) is kept with ASV; the MT second person nāṭaštāh is kept against the LXX third person. (4) At 2:12 MT wᵉšāp̄ēl is kept; the emendation wᵉḡāḇōah (BHS; Wildberger) is reported in commentary. (5) ʿāraṣ means 'terrify, inspire awe' (BDB; HALOT), the sense it has at Isa 8:12-13, 29:23 and 47:12; ASV's 'shake mightily' is not supported by that usage, and NRSV 'terrify' and NJPS 'overawe' are followed. (6) At 2:20 the Leningrad Codex divides laḥpōr pērôṯ 'to dig holes', with no ketiv/qere note in the WLC encoding; BDB and the BHS apparatus record the one-word reading of many manuscripts and the versions, and ASV, NRSV and NJPS translate it. The consonants are unchanged, but because the word division departs from the base text the item is also recorded under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah as a word-division exception (founder sign-off 2026-11-26).
entry.rendering: 2:2 'on the top of the mountains … shall flow to it' (ASV); 2:4 'shall decide for many peoples … plowshares' (ASV/NJPS); 2:6 'they are full from the east' with no supplement, 'they strike hands with' (spq I), MT 2ms 'you have forsaken' kept; 2:12 MT wᵉšāp̄ēl 'and it shall be brought low' kept (emendation gāḇōah in commentary); 2:19, 21 laʿărōṣ 'to terrify' (NRSV; ASV 'shake mightily'); 2:20 one-word reading laḥăp̄arpērôṯ 'to the moles' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS) against the Leningrad two-word division.
